theory.mqtt: MQTT (Message Queuing Telemetry Transport) is a lightweight messaging protocol ideal for IoT. Uses publish-subscribe pattern where devices publish messages to topics and others subscribe to receive them.
theory.broker: MQTT broker is central server that receives all messages and distributes to subscribers. Examples: Mosquitto, HiveMQ, EMQX. Can be local or cloud-based.
theory.topics: Topics are hierarchical strings separated by /. Example: home/living_room/temperature. Supports wildcards: + (single level) and # (multiple levels).
theory.qos: QoS (Quality of Service) defines delivery guarantee: 0 (at most once), 1 (at least once), 2 (exactly once).

solutions: Check if broker is accessible (ping IP)
Confirm port 1883 is open (use telnet ip 1883)
Make sure on same network (if local broker)
Check credentials if broker requires authentication
Test with mosquitto_sub in terminal: mosquitto_sub -h IP -t '#'
Use wildcard # to test all topics
Check QoS (use 1 to guarantee delivery in tests)
Monitor with MQTT Explorer to see all messages
Test sensor standalone before MQTT integration
Check if common cathode or anode
Test each color individually (R, G, B)
Validate JSON format of received messages
